sections.h2: Which Boyd County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three do. The Property Valuation Administrator assesses, the Sheriff's Office collects the current year's bill, and the County Clerk takes over delinquent bills from earlier years.

The county's Property Valuation page says the PVA values all real and personal property in Boyd County, except items the Kentucky Department of Revenue assigns itself, such as public service companies, bank shares and vehicles. The PVA's mailing address is PO Box 434, Catlettsburg, KY 41129. For a house, the PVA's number is the starting point of everything else on the bill.

sections.h2: What is Boyd County's tax base like?
sections.html:
Boyd County is compact, about 160 square miles of land with more than 300 people per square mile, and 76.2% of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census. The estimated 2025 population was 47,751 in about 21,818 housing units.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median owner-occupied value of $130,700, a median household income of $61,118 and 70.2% of homes owner-occupied. A Boyd County sale price near that median means a taxable assessment far below the Bluegrass counties, though the 911 service fee and city levies still appear on the bill.

  • Ashland and Catlettsburg bill their own city property tax, and you call the city, not the county.
  • The county bill lists a 911 service fee, with questions going to Boyd County 911 at 606-329-2191.
  • Three school districts cover different parts of the county: Boyd County Public Schools, Ashland Independent and Fairview Independent.

sections.h2: When are Boyd County property taxes due?
sections.html:
State law sets the schedule the Sheriff's Office follows. Tax is due by December 31 of the assessment year, with a discount for paying early and penalties for paying late.

Kentucky property tax payment schedule under KRS 134.015, applied by the Boyd County Sheriff
Payment timingResult
By November 12% discount
November 2 to December 31Face amount, no penalty
January 1 to January 315% penalty
After January 3110% penalty

The county's property tax page says online viewing and payment are available through the Sheriff's Office. Dates on a printed bill can run later than the statute's calendar when the state allows an alternative collection schedule, so read the bill and ask the sheriff's office which dates apply to your parcel. When the sheriff's collection period ends, unpaid prior year taxes move to the County Clerk, who handles them at 606-739-5116, option 4.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Boyd County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA. The assessment date is January 1, and a notice of change is mailed when a property's value goes up from the year before.

The Boyd County PVA's appeals page explains the order of steps. You first schedule a conference with the PVA or a deputy before the tax roll inspection period ends. That period normally begins the first Monday in May and runs six days a week for two weeks, ending on the third Monday in May, though it can be adjusted. Under KRS 133.120 the next step is a written petition to the County Clerk for a hearing by the board of assessment appeals.

  • Bring comparable sales, an appraisal, photos of damage or a contractor's repair estimate.
  • Telephone conferences are allowed on request.
  • The petition must give your reasons and your opinion of the property's fair cash value.
  • Keep paying: an appeal does not delay collection of the tax.

sections.h2: Does Boyd County have a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Kentucky's exemption applies in Boyd County for homeowners who are 65 or older or totally disabled. The state value is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, deducted from the assessed value of the home.

You file the application with the Boyd County PVA. Age can be shown with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. A disability claim needs proof of classification as totally disabled under a federal or retirement system program, and it is renewed each year unless the owner is a service-connected disabled veteran or has been found totally and permanently disabled.

sections.h2: Who can speak for me in a Boyd County assessment appeal?
sections.html:
You can appear yourself, or you can use an agent. Kentucky law limits who may be paid to represent an owner at a PVA conference or a board hearing.

  • An attorney or a certified public accountant.
  • A tax consultant or a Kentucky licensed real estate broker or sales associate.
  • An employee of the property owner.
  • A licensed or certified Kentucky real property appraiser.

The agent must bring written authorization from the owner and disclose any personal interest, including a contingency fee. If the county board rules against you, you may appeal to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, but only if you went through the county board first.

sections.h2: What does a late Boyd County payment cost on a sample bill?
sections.html:
Use a bill of $1,000 for illustration. Paid by November 1 it is $980. Paid from November 2 through December 31 it is $1,000. In January the 5% penalty brings it to $1,050, and after January 31 the 10% statutory penalty brings it to $1,100. Other charges can attach once a bill is turned over to the clerk, so ask that office for a payoff before closing.

These figures show the statute's calendar only. Your own bill carries the county, school and district amounts plus the 911 fee, and the Sheriff's Office can tell you the exact total for your parcel.

sections.h2: What else do Census numbers show about Boyd County owners?
sections.html:
The county's poverty rate was 18.0% in the Census figures, and 17.2% of residents under 65 reported a disability. Median owner costs were $1,217 a month with a mortgage and $463 without one, and 85.9% of residents had lived in the same house a year earlier.

For an owner on a fixed income, the homestead exemption and an on-time payment in the discount window matter more than a small difference in value. A seller in that position should read the bill's due dates before listing and ask the PVA whether an exemption application is on file for the home.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Boyd County house with taxes owed?
sections.html:
The tax is the taxpayer's personal debt from the assessment date, and a lien follows the property once the tax turns delinquent, so a title company will not close over an unpaid bill. The payoff is simply added to the closing statement.

  • Current year unpaid: contact the Sheriff's Office for the exact amount and any penalty.
  • Prior years unpaid: contact the County Clerk's office.
  • City tax: ask the City of Ashland at 606-385-3275 or the City of Catlettsburg at 606-739-5223.
  • Escrow lenders: ask whether they have already paid the bill.

If the bill cannot be paid before the sale, ask the closing agent to pay it from your proceeds at the table.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Boyd County?
faqs.a: The Boyd County Sheriff's Office collects the current year's tax. The County Clerk collects delinquent taxes from prior years.

faqs.q: What is the Boyd County property tax discount?
faqs.a: State law gives a 2% discount for paying in full by November 1 of the assessment year, then face amount through December 31. Check your bill for the exact dates.

faqs.q: How do I pay delinquent Boyd County property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the Boyd County Clerk's office at 606-739-5116 and press option 4, or use the clerk's website.

faqs.q: When can I meet with the Boyd County PVA about my assessment?
faqs.a: The conference must be held before or during the tax roll inspection period, which normally starts on the first Monday in May and ends on the third Monday in May.

faqs.q: Do Ashland and Catlettsburg charge their own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Questions about city property tax go to the City of Ashland at 606-385-3275 or the City of Catlettsburg at 606-739-5223.
